summary: No findings. The only untrusted input is the local developer's CLI argument (process.argv.slice(2)) to tools/chart-print/main.ts. chartPrintMain rejects more than one argument, then looks the size up with Object.hasOwn on the plain-object literal PREFLOP_CHARTS, so prototype keys such as toString, __proto__ and constructor are rejected (a unit test covers toString). The argument is never used as a path, in a shell command, or as a template/regex source. Unknown values go back only to the caller's own stderr, and the exit code is 2. Echoing terminal control characters there would only affect the person who typed them, so there's no trust boundary to cross. The acceptance test uses spawnSync('npm', [...]) with an argument array and no shell: true, and only passes fixed literal sizes, so there's no shell injection path. It reads chart JSON from fixed repo paths. No new dependencies, secrets, randomness, temp files or unbounded input.
